\textbf{to be, to exist, to stay — and the negative Telugu has to fetch from a different verb}\enspace\emph{\te{ఉండు}}\enspace(uṇḍu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: pronunciation, grammar; \hyperref[ch:te-core-verbs]{Chapter~32, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-core-verbs}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to be, to stay, to live}\enspace\emph{\te{ఉండు}}\enspace(uṇḍu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, grammar, etymology; \hyperref[ch:first-verbs]{Chapter~5, p.~\pageref*{ch:first-verbs}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to come — the command is \te{రా}, but every ending attaches to \te{వచ్చు} instead}\enspace\emph{\te{రా}}\enspace(rā)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: grammar; \hyperref[ch:te-core-verbs]{Chapter~32, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-core-verbs}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to eat — the inherited Dravidian root Telugu kept as its plain everyday verb, with the mealtime nouns borrowed from Sanskrit}\enspace\emph{\te{తిను}}\enspace(tinu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: etymology; \hyperref[ch:te-core-verbs]{Chapter~32, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-core-verbs}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to go (and \te{వచ్చు}, to come)}\enspace\emph{\te{వెళ్ళు}}\enspace(veḷḷu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: pronunciation, script, etymology; \hyperref[ch:farewells]{Chapter~4, p.~\pageref*{ch:farewells}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to go — with one tense-piece covering both \textquotedblleft{}I go\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}I will go\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}right now\textquotedblright{} built out of the be-verb}\enspace\emph{\te{వెళ్ళు}}\enspace(veḷḷu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: pronunciation, grammar; \hyperref[ch:te-core-verbs]{Chapter~32, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-core-verbs}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to help — a Sanskrit noun on the native do-verb, and the noun takes apart into \textquotedblleft{}a going with somebody\textquotedblright{}}\enspace\emph{\te{సహాయం} \te{చేయు}}\enspace(sahāyaṁ cēyu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, etymology, usage and culture; \hyperref[ch:te-verbs-between-people]{Chapter~34, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-verbs-between-people}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to read — and, with no second word, to study; the same form is the noun for an education, and its middle vowel moves as the endings change}\enspace\emph{\te{చదువు}}\enspace(caduvu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, grammar; \hyperref[ch:te-verbs-of-the-mind]{Chapter~33, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-verbs-of-the-mind}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to see, to look — Telugu's own everyday see-word, and the respectful -\te{అండి} ending that fits any verb stem}\enspace\emph{\te{చూడు}}\enspace(cūḍu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: pronunciation, grammar; \hyperref[ch:te-core-verbs]{Chapter~32, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-core-verbs}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to speak}\enspace\emph{\te{మాట్లాడు}}\enspace(māṭlāḍu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: pronunciation, script, grammar, etymology; \hyperref[ch:first-verbs]{Chapter~5, p.~\pageref*{ch:first-verbs}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to take — \te{తీయు}, \textquotedblleft{}to pull out\textquotedblright{}, wearing the same -\te{కో} as the last chapter's two mind-verbs, so taking is pulling something out for yourself}\enspace\emph{\te{తీసుకో}}\enspace(tīsukō)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, grammar, etymology; \hyperref[ch:te-verbs-between-people]{Chapter~34, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-verbs-between-people}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to think — literally \textquotedblleft{}say it to yourself\textquotedblright{}, built from the family's say-verb plus the ending that turns a verb back on its own doer}\enspace\emph{\te{అనుకో}}\enspace(anukō)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, grammar, etymology; \hyperref[ch:te-verbs-of-the-mind]{Chapter~33, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-verbs-of-the-mind}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to understand — \textquotedblleft{}make the meaning your own\textquotedblright{}, a Sanskrit noun on the native do-verb with the ending that hands the action back to you}\enspace\emph{\te{అర్థం} \te{చేసుకో}}\enspace(arthaṁ cēsukō)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, grammar, etymology; \hyperref[ch:te-verbs-of-the-mind]{Chapter~33, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-verbs-of-the-mind}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to work (lit. \textquotedblleft{}work-do\textquotedblright{})}\enspace\emph{\te{పని} \te{చేయు}}\enspace(pani cēyu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, grammar, etymology; \hyperref[ch:first-verbs]{Chapter~5, p.~\pageref*{ch:first-verbs}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{to write — an old Dravidian word for drawing a line, still spelled \te{వ్రాయు} in books, and the chapter's fourth mind-verb}\enspace\emph{\te{రాయు}}\enspace(rāyu)\par
\footnotesize explicit focus: script, grammar, etymology; \hyperref[ch:te-verbs-of-the-mind]{Chapter~33, p.~\pageref*{ch:te-verbs-of-the-mind}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright
\textbf{water (matching Tamil/Kannada's neer/niiru), and rice raw/cooked — completing the family's water and rice pattern}\enspace\emph{\te{నీళ్ళు} \te{బియ్యం} \te{అన్నం}}\par

\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright

\footnotesize explicit focus: script, etymology; \hyperref[ch:farewells]{Chapter~4, p.~\pageref*{ch:farewells}}

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright

\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\noindent\begin{minipage}[t]{\linewidth}
\raggedright

\footnotesize explicit focus: pronunciation, script, etymology; \hyperref[ch:responding]{Chapter~3, p.~\pageref*{ch:responding}}
\end{minipage}\par\smallskip

\raggedright
\textbf{what}\enspace\emph{\te{ఏమిటి}}\enspace(ēmiṭi)\par

\end{minipage}\par\smallskip
